purpose: Resolve the current Triggerword-5 open gate for stern.py consolidation/effect-path chronology and bounded historical Project-Frankenstein predecessor mapping without minting runtime or causal credit from source history.
evidence_boundary: This run inspected exact current source, exact Git commit history, and pinned historical dossier/source manifests. It did not re-execute Frankenstein runtime behavior. Commit messages that report prior live tests are retained as historical/runtime-receipt claims of those commits, not independently reproduced by this run.

semantic_atoms.finding: stern.py declares the Phase-1 consolidation boundary: hook/session/retrieval/config/room/digest responsibilities were collapsed into one hook/CLI control plane around unified.db, while the model is explicitly prohibited from writing unified.db directly; writes are event-triggered through code with evidence.
semantic_atoms.frankenstein2_implication: Preserve one deterministic state/effect authority boundary, but do not equate authority unification with physical single-file implementation.

semantic_atoms.finding: The same current source records deliberate external exceptions: abruf/paket.py remains external, and a selftest discovered that fully inlining/removing wegehierarchie.py silently disabled paket.py F94 reinforcement because paket.py imports it directly.
semantic_atoms.frankenstein2_implication: Consolidation must be dependency-closure tested. Specialized modules may remain outside the authority core when their boundary is explicit and mechanically verified.

semantic_atoms.finding: The repository mirror had fallen behind the live star tree: stern.py reportedly grew from 8123 to 12019 lines across PHASE 9-24 on the development host before the repository was resynchronized. The same commit preserved fresh-install and dead-import defects instead of silently claiming repository/runtime equivalence.
semantic_atoms.frankenstein2_implication: Every effect/control claim needs exact source identity. Live host state and repository state must not be treated as interchangeable without a synchronization receipt.

semantic_atoms.finding: Realtime conversation moved stern dispatch from subprocess.run to direct in-process function dispatch after an intermittent 15-20+ second fork/exec deadlock with live PortAudio streams. The commit reports real read/write-path verification and service restart checks.
semantic_atoms.causal_caution: This run does not independently reproduce that receipt; the chronology establishes an implementation transition and the historical report attached to it.

semantic_atoms.finding: The in-process transition changed configuration-cache lifetime semantics. A module-global cache that was harmless in short-lived CLI processes became persistent in the daemon, so externally written gespraech.aktiv/voice-loop changes were not observed until restart. The commit reports a direct reproduction and a targeted cache-invalidation repair.
semantic_atoms.frankenstein2_implication: Process-topology changes are semantic changes. Long-lived GRID/voice/visual organs need explicit configuration generation/invalidation semantics rather than accidental process-lifetime freshness.

semantic_atoms.finding: The in-process initiative-episode dispatcher initially failed to forward outcome_json even though callers supplied it; prior rows were observed with outcome_json='{}' despite non-trivial payloads. The repair forwards outcome_json plus voice_event_kind and routes disagreement through post-action visual re-look/capsule refresh.
semantic_atoms.frankenstein2_implication: A successful state write is not sufficient evidence of effect/result re-entry. Typed dispatcher completeness must be checked field-by-field from request through journal/outcome re-entry.

semantic_atoms.finding: A live unified.db schema lag reportedly caused embedding writes to fail silently and semantic search to raise sqlite3.OperationalError. The repair added an idempotent migration that rebuilt the table because the target composite UNIQUE constraint could not be added correctly with a simple ALTER COLUMN path.
semantic_atoms.frankenstein2_implication: Typed state/effect paths require schema-generation compatibility and migration evidence before a write path is credited.

bounded_findings: Historical module families included core orchestration/context/effects, inference routing, local model lifecycle, planner/executor/tools, multiple memory families, vision, voice, rooms, and safety/recovery/audit mechanisms.
The historical system autopsy reports many SQLite/service authorities and explicitly identifies integration-surface multiplicity as a pressure that later favored UnifiedDB.

The reusable historical effect lesson is the separation of tool invocation from verified real effect/result; current research artifacts must not back-project modern effect authority onto the old system without exact source evidence.

forensic_synthesis: The strongest continuity is not a monolithic stern.py file; it is a state-first control/evidence boundary around one durable substrate plus explicit adapters.

The strongest negative lineage is boundary-semantic drift: repository/live divergence, hidden import dependencies, process-lifetime cache changes, incomplete dispatch payload forwarding, and schema drift all produced failures while individual components could still appear locally healthy.

For Frankenstein 2.0 / GRID10, central authority should therefore be implemented as typed contracts with exact source/generation/provenance and outcome completeness, while specialized sensors/cognition modules remain replaceable organs.
Effect request, dispatch success, durable journal row, observed world outcome, and verified re-entry must remain distinct evidence states.
